# queue_enqueue

Puts a change (head, with its first-parent chain since base) in target's landing queue and starts its runner: the entry lands once a check of it on the target's head passes (the repository's check, .swarmops/workspaces.json), with no other call. Pass a key to make a retry safe; wait for it with queue\_wait.

```yaml
title: "queue_enqueue"
description: "Queue a change to land."
since: "0.13.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
cli_command: "swarmops queue enqueue"
envelope_op: "queue_enqueue"
request_type: "QueueEnqueueReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":false}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `QueueEnqueueReq`: `swarmops schema QueueEnqueueReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base` | string or null | no |  | Where the change starts: a first-parent ancestor of `head`. When omitted, the merge base of `head` and the target's head. |
| `head` | string | yes |  | The change's head. A revision as the caller wrote it, for the store to resolve: a ref name (`main`, `release/1.2`), a full 64-hex changeset id or a unique prefix of at least 12 hex digits, or a ref's earlier value: `<ref>@{N}` the value it held N moves before its current one (`@{0}` is the current value), `<ref>@{at=<unix seconds>}` the value set by its newest move recorded at or before that instant (the writer's clock, moves read in journal order); optionally followed by `~N` for the N-th first-parent ancestor. |
| `key` | string or null | no |  | Makes a retry safe: at most 128 bytes. The same key with the same target, head and base answers the entry it made; with another, `E_INVALID_ARG` (`details.reason` `key_reused`). When omitted, each enqueue makes a new entry. |
| `target` | string | yes |  | The ref to land on, which must exist. |

## Annotations

It adds to the store and changes nothing there. Run again, a `commit` adds again, another changeset signed at its own time, unless the call carries an `idempotency_key`, which makes the same call again a replay; a `blob_put` of the same content finds it stored, and says so in its result.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `false` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `false` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `false` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `false` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops queue enqueue`](../commands/queue-enqueue.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

## Examples

### MCP

```json
{
  "id": 2,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "arguments": {
      "head": "[first]",
      "key": "k-1",
      "target": "main"
    },
    "name": "queue_enqueue"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "id": 2,
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "text": "{\"api\":1,\"meta\":{\"auth\":\"trust\",\"elapsed_ms\":\"[elapsed_ms]\",\"repo\":\"[tmp]/store\",\"resolved\":{\"[first]\":\"[first]\",\"main\":\"[main]\"}},\"ok\":true,\"op\":\"queue_enqueue\",\"result\":{\"entry\":{\"base\":\"[main]\",\"head\":\"[first]\",\"id\":\"[entry1]\",\"key\":\"k-1\",\"position\":1,\"state\":\"waiting\",\"target\":\"main\"},\"replayed\":false}}",
        "type": "text"
      }
    ],
    "isError": false,
    "structuredContent": {
      "api": 1,
      "meta": {
        "auth": "trust",
        "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
        "repo": "[tmp]/store",
        "resolved": {
          "[first]": "[first]",
          "main": "[main]"
        }
      },
      "ok": true,
      "op": "queue_enqueue",
      "result": {
        "entry": {
          "base": "[main]",
          "head": "[first]",
          "id": "[entry1]",
          "key": "k-1",
          "position": 1,
          "state": "waiting",
          "target": "main"
        },
        "replayed": false
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The server ran as `swarmops mcp --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17`, after `initialize`. Recorded by the MCP tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time, the version.

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `queue_enqueue`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops queue enqueue`](../commands/queue-enqueue.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `QueueEnqueueReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED`](../errors.md#e_identity_required): the server runs with no identity.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops queue enqueue`](../commands/queue-enqueue.md#errors) lists them.
